paragraphs: In Bereshit Rabbah, chapter פ״סב־כב (supplied 62:22; corresponding saved digital narrative at 65:22), and Midrash Tehillim, end of chapter 11: It is told of him that he was the son of the sister of Yose ben Yoezer of Tzereidah (of the Pairs), and he went astray. He was riding a horse on the Sabbath, and a beam was carried before him on which to hang his uncle. He said to him: See the horse my master has mounted me on (he served idols), and see the horse your Master has mounted you on! He answered him: If this is so for those who anger Him, all the more so for those who do His will. He said to him: Has any person done His will more than you? He replied: If this is so for those who do His will, all the more so for those who anger Him. The matter entered him like the venom of a snake, and he went and carried out upon himself the four death penalties of the court. Yose ben Yoezer dozed off and saw his bier flying in the air; he said: In a short moment this one has preceded me to the Garden of Eden. And see the entry Yose ben Yoezer.

notes.text: The Bereshit Rabbah locator is printed פ״סב־כב; its exact chapter designation is unclear.

The supplied Bereshit Rabbah locator פ״סב־כב reads 62:22; the whole saved Midrash Rabbah -- TE scalar is labeled 65:22 and spells the name יקום, whereas Hyman has יקים. Both locators and spellings remain distinct; this digital match does not prove a printing or OCR error. The separate Midrash Tehillim end-of-chapter-11 reference remains unresolved: the old bounded checks of 11:6, 11:7 and 12:1 are historical nonmatches, not global absence. The full Rabbi title in the named primary passage is not imported into Hyman’s untitled Yose ben Yoezer occurrences. Hyman explicitly says sister’s son and uncle, retains his of-the-Pairs and he-served-idols parentheses, both conditional kal-vachomer arguments and the genuine Has any person done His will more than you? question. Each master mounts his own rider; the earlier reversal is preserved only in historical English. The snake-venom image, four court death penalties, Yose’s dozing, flying bier and Garden of Eden conclusion remain. The longer named primary passage contains additional narrative and details absent from Hyman; none are imported. The heading, all older notes and source hold remain unchanged.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume II, printed p. 803, retains Yakim (יקים) and the Bereshit Rabbah locator פ״סב־כב, alongside Midrash Tehillim at the end of chapter 11. The matching whole TE Bereshit Rabbah passage is labeled 65:22 and names Yakum (יקום). A newly consulted whole OYW Midrash Tehillim paragraph, digitally numbered 11:7, also explicitly names Yakum, his relationship to Yose ben Yoezer, the horse dialogue, both conditional arguments, the four court death penalties and the flying bier. This recovers the second cited parallel; the earlier note about its being unlocated describes the preceding bounded checks. The narrative’s longer details are not inserted into Hyman’s abridgment. The different name forms and Bereshit Rabbah locators remain visible, without a new identification or a claim about how the discrepancy arose.
